title: CI downloads and executes the Odin compiler tarball with no checksum verification
detail: The Odin tarball is curl'd from GitHub, extracted and executed with no sha256 check. The pin (.odin-version = dev-2026-08) is a mutable dev tag; a tampered or re-cut release silently runs a malicious compiler that builds and tests every PR.
recommended_fix: Record a sha256 for the pinned asset and verify after curl (printf '%s  odin.tar.gz' "$EXPECTED" | shasum -a 256 -c) before any tar/exec. Prefer an immutable release artifact or commit-pinned checksum.

title: raylib source cloned by mutable git tag instead of a pinned commit sha
detail: raylib is fetched by its (mutable) release tag and compiled into libraylib_sw.a, linked into the harness. If the tag moved the rebuilt binary would silently change. raylib release tags are stable in practice, so risk is low.
recommended_fix: Pin to the immutable commit sha the 6.0 tag resolves to: clone then `git checkout <sha>` (or record the sha and verify it post-fetch), instead of cloning by tag name.
